title: Controlling Product Selectivity Toward Methanol in Plasma Catalytic Dry Methane Reforming Using Oxygen Co-Feeding
content: Direct conversion of methane (CH₄) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) into oxygenated products remains challenging because of the high stability of both molecules and the complexity of controlling product selectivity. This study investigated oxygen-assisted non-thermal plasma (NTP)-catalytic dry methane reforming (DMR) for directing product formation toward methanol. Plasma-only, 13X, and Co/13X were evaluated using oxygen co-feeding at a CH4: CO2: O2 ratio of 3:1:1.3. Under conventional DMR conditions (CH4: CO2 = 3:1), product distributions were dominated by syngas and light hydrocarbons, while methanol selectivity remained below 3.33%. Oxygen addition substantially modified the product distribution, increasing methanol selectivity to 10.95%, 15.27%, and 18.14% for plasma-only, 13X, and Co/13X configurations, respectively. Optical emission spectroscopy revealed increased emission from excited atomic oxygen (777 nm), supporting the proposed contribution of oxygen plasma mediated reaction pathways. Furthermore, Physio-chemical, XPS and FTIR surface analyses indicated reduced carbon accumulation following oxygen addition. These findings demonstrated that oxygen co-feeding, particularly in combination with Co/13X, provided an effective approach for enhancing methanol selectivity during plasma-assisted DMR. The results highlighted the potential of feed-composition engineering and plasma-catalyst interactions for directing methane and CO₂ conversion toward targeted oxygenated products.
